convoLines.text: "I hate to ask this, but I can't shake it. I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"The fever's not breaking and I'm barely keeping food down. I need help — real help, not just water."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Giuseppe owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I hate to ask this, but whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"I'm burning up and there's nothing left in me. Someone who knows sickness — please."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Giuseppe always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I don't know what to do with my hands today."
Vincent has an edge today — something curdled.
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"Oh." A long pause. "I wasn't a hotel housekeeper. I was an army medic. I wanted an edge. You were new, you were listening, and I used it. I'm not proud of that." Vincent won't meet your eyes.
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"I — I don't remember saying that." A beat. "People hear what they want to hear."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I got lost in it for a second. What did you want to ask? Easy."
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"Take your time."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on that question. ...sorry."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About the sickness I'm fighting — still need hands. Are you in?"
"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."
As I said — Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Nicole always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"...Actually, forget it."
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the far treeline, past the rocks — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
Done — their story has a crack in it now.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
"Rest when you can. We'll talk again soon."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about that favor — that was 8 days back. Still on your mind? 'As I said — Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.'"
Another pass over the same ground. Somebody's being careful. Careful people leave cleaner trails — and cleaner trails are still trails.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"I'm burning up and there's nothing left in me. Someone who knows sickness — please."
"The fever's not breaking and I'm barely keeping food down. I need help — real help, not just water."
As I said — Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Watch this — Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"Oh." A long pause. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. Everyone out here is selling something. I was selling a better version of me." Vincent won't meet your eyes.
"That again?" Vincent sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
*Confessions need weight behind them. What you have right now is a thread. Find the rope.*
Vincent blinks, then groans. "Oh, that's my fault, I worded that terribly. What I meant was..." The real version is boring, which is how you know it's true.
"Still on their secret."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Go on, then. I'll be thinking good thoughts at you."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I don't pray, exactly. But I talk to the sky sometimes. It hasn't answered yet."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the ridge above the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

deathBeat: d6: 🕯️ Giuseppe Gu is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d7: That night, they bring Giuseppe home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d7: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.

d8: ◈ THE SPARK — something clicks. A trick Aki learned long ago suddenly has edges it never had. SYSTEM: "ANOMALY: organic unit demonstrates pattern recognition. Slot capacity increased. We are taking notes." (Ability slots: 2)

d8: ◈ SYSTEM: "RATINGS DIP. The audience wants STAKES — pointed ones. A PALISADE. Stockpile 14,000 kcal, 350 wood and 60 stone. Walls make such good television. You will thank us when the teeth come."
d8: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 35. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 3."
burialWindowSay: d7: That night, they bring Giuseppe home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d7: 📻 "Why do the small humans keep putting organic matter in their FACE-HOLES? We built you a fusion pellet! ...You BURIED it. WHY did you bury the pellet?!"
d8: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+6 integration)
d9: You say a few words for them. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d9: Burying the bloating dead was honest work, and it cost you. Fever by nightfall. (-10 health)
d9: You bury them. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
